YOUR ANGLE: **Efficiency**. Flag wasted work this diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O, independent operations done sequentially that needn't be, work added to a hot/startup path, or re-reading something already in hand.

Specific things worth checking:
- driver/cmd_run.cpp run_fast: `elf_xlen(cli.positional[0])` opens+reads the ELF. Is it called even when an explicit `--engine qemu32/qemu64` makes the result unused (i.e. could it be computed only when needed)? Is the same ELF read multiple times across run_fast/run_accurate/run_hybrid for a single invocation?

- runtime/Makefile: does the rv32 path rebuild things unnecessarily?

Read the actual files to confirm before claiming. Output a concise list; each item: `file:line` - one-line finding - the cheaper alternative - cost. If genuinely clean, say so. Do NOT edit any files; I apply fixes myself. Quality review, not a correctness-bug hunt.

commit 3fd0ffaa17c0b2c5ced6ca69ae1dc574bba8e969
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Mon Jun 29 21:34:44 2026 +0800

    feat: rv32 support across run, runtime, and fixtures
    
    andesim now treats rv32 as a first-class peer of rv64, driven by the ELF's
    class byte (e_ident[EI_CLASS]). See docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md.
    
    Run dispatch (driver/):
    - elf_xlen() reads an ELF's width (32/64). fast auto-picks
      qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (explicit --engine wins + warns on a
      conflict); cycle and hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen
      via one shared elf_engine_arch_error -- a clear up-front message instead of
      the engine's cryptic "not of ELFCLASSxx".
    
    Dual-arch runtime (runtime/, config, scripts):
    - runtime/Makefile parameterized by ARCH: rv64 -> build/runtime,
      rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32 (rv32gc/ilp32d, riscv32-unknown-elf-).
    - Real rv64-isms fixed: vplat_syscalls.c L2-cache flush guarded to rv64
      (#if __riscv_xlen==64); handler.c trap CSRs made XLEN-wide, which also fixes
      latent rv64 mepc/mtval truncation and the interrupt-bit test.
    - HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 config var (a second, separate toolchain);
      build_runtime.sh builds both arches (and its stale artifact names fixed);
      build_all.sh runtime delegates to it.
    
    rv32 fixtures (tests/fixtures/):
    - make rv32 -> rv32_spin (asm) + rv32_c_hello (C, links the rv32 runtime),
      reusing existing sources.
    
    Docs: USER_GUIDE sec 1.3 (two toolchains) + new sec 5.1 (rv32 link command and
    the arch-match rules).
    
    Tested (TDD, RED first): elf_xlen unit (driver/elf_syms_test.cpp);
    test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh (both arch directions, incl. a real rv32_c_hello
    run on qemu-system-riscv32); test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh (both runtime
    classes). rv64 fixtures and the fast/cycle/hybrid suites stay green.
    Behavioral change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
+#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
+#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
+#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
+# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
+#
+# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
+# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
+# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
+CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
+CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
+
+[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
+ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
+ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
+if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
+  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
+    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
+      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
+    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
+    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
+  fi
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
+fi
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
+
+# rv64 (required).
+if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
+echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
+
+# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
+if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
+  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Build the user-facing andesim runtime (runtime/) for both arches. Produces:
+#   build/runtime/       libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o, andesim.ld, andesim.specs,
+#                        include/andesim/ROI.h   (rv64; link -B build/runtime)
+#   build/runtime/rv32/  the same, rv32          (rv32; link -B build/runtime/rv32)
+# Users link with `-B <dir> -specs=andesim.specs` (USER_GUIDE.md section 5).
+#
+# rv64 always builds (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). rv32 builds too when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32
+# is set. Self-contained: fills either toolchain from config.env (exported env
+# wins), like setup.sh, so it runs without `source ./setup.sh` first.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+SRC="$ROOT/runtime"
+CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
+CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"
+
+[[ -f "$SRC/Makefile" ]] || { echo "missing $SRC/Makefile" >&2; exit 1; }
+
+# Capture exported values (they win), then source config.env to fill any gaps.
+ENV_TC64="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}"
+ENV_TC32="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}"
+if [[ -z "$ENV_TC64" || -z "$ENV_TC32" ]]; then
+  if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
+    [[ -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]] \
+      || { echo "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE" >&2; exit 1; }
+    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
+    echo "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchains live elsewhere" >&2
+  fi
+  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
+  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
+fi
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC64" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$ENV_TC64"
+[[ -n "$ENV_TC32" ]] && HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32="$ENV_TC32"
+
+# rv64 (required).
+if [[ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" || ! -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  echo "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset or has no bin/; check $CONFIG_FILE" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv64 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"
+echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a (rv64)"
+
+# rv32 (optional: needs the second toolchain).
+if [[ -n "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}" && -d "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32:-}/bin" ]]; then
+  make -C "$SRC" ARCH=rv32 TOOLCHAIN="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32"
+  echo "built: $ROOT/build/runtime/rv32/libandesim_runtime.a (rv32)"

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass `TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain` on the command line)
endif
CC        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures (docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md F3) ---------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                 $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                 $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

1	# Build the user-facing andesim runtime library into build/runtime/:
2	#
3	#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
4	#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
5	#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
6	#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
7	#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
8	#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
9	#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
10	#
11	# Users link with:
12	#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
13	# or, without the gcc driver:
14	#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
15	#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
16	#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
17	#
18	# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
19	# tests/fixtures/Makefile.
20	
21	# ARCH selects the target width: rv64 (default) or rv32. Each arch has its own
22	# toolchain (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32), triple, -march/-mabi, and
23	# output dir. rv64 stays at build/runtime (back-compat with `-B build/runtime`);
24	# rv32 lands at build/runtime/rv32 (`-B build/runtime/rv32`).
25	ARCH ?= rv64
26	
27	ifeq ($(ARCH),rv64)
28	  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
29	  TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
30	  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d
31	  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime
32	else ifeq ($(ARCH),rv32)
33	  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
34	  TRIPLE    := riscv32-unknown-elf
35	  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d
36	  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime/rv32
37	else
38	  $(error ARCH must be rv64 or rv32, got '$(ARCH)')
39	endif
40	
41	ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
42	$(error No toolchain for ARCH=$(ARCH). Set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (rv64) / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (rv32) in config.env, `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
43	endif
44	
45	CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
46	AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar
47	
48	# rvNNgc objects link cleanly into rvNNgcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V arch
49	# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants of the arch.
50	CFLAGS := $(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall
51	
52	LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o
53	
54	.PHONY: all clean
55	
56	all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
57	     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h
58	
59	$(OUT):
60		mkdir -p $@
61	
62	$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
63		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
64	
65	$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
66		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
67	
68	$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h
69	
70	$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
71		$(AR) rcs $@ $^
72	
73	$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
74		cp $< $@
75	
76	$(OUT)/andesim.specs: andesim.specs | $(OUT)
77		cp $< $@
78	
79	# gcc adds <-B prefix>/include to the include path, so the two-flag user
80	# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
81	$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
82		mkdir -p $(dir $@)
83		cp $< $@
84	
85	clean:
86		rm -rf $(OUT)

#   libandesim_runtime.a   trap.o handler.o vplat_syscalls.o
#   crt0.o                   startfile; kept OUTSIDE the archive because
#                            nothing references _start, so the linker
#                            would never extract it from a .a (same
#                            reason toolchains ship crt0.o next to libc.a)
#   andesim.ld             linker script (load base 0x00100000)
#   include/andesim/ROI.h  ROI markers (HINT NOPs; same dir rides -B)
#
# Users link with:
#   gcc ... -B <repo>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs hello.c
# or, without the gcc driver:
#   gcc ... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T andesim.ld crt0.o hello.c \
#       -L <repo>/build/runtime \
#       -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
#
# Toolchain location comes from config.env (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN), same as
# tests/fixtures/Makefile.

# ARCH selects the target width: rv64 (default) or rv32. Each arch has its own
# toolchain (HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32), triple, -march/-mabi, and
# output dir. rv64 stays at build/runtime (back-compat with `-B build/runtime`);
# rv32 lands at build/runtime/rv32 (`-B build/runtime/rv32`).
ARCH ?= rv64

ifeq ($(ARCH),rv64)
  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
  TRIPLE    := riscv64-unknown-elf
  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d
  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime
else ifeq ($(ARCH),rv32)
  TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
  TRIPLE    := riscv32-unknown-elf
  ARCHFLAGS := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d
  OUT       ?= ../build/runtime/rv32
else
  $(error ARCH must be rv64 or rv32, got '$(ARCH)')
endif

ifeq ($(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),)
$(error No toolchain for ARCH=$(ARCH). Set HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN (rv64) / HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 (rv32) in config.env, `source ./setup.sh`, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path)
endif

CC := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-gcc
AR := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/$(TRIPLE)-ar

# rvNNgc objects link cleanly into rvNNgcv programs (ld unions the RISC-V arch
# attributes), so one build serves both -march variants of the arch.
CFLAGS := $(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall

LIB_OBJS := $(OUT)/trap.o $(OUT)/handler.o $(OUT)/vplat_syscalls.o

.PHONY: all clean

all: $(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a $(OUT)/crt0.o $(OUT)/andesim.ld \
     $(OUT)/andesim.specs $(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h

$(OUT):
	mkdir -p $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.S | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/%.o: %.c | $(OUT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OUT)/trap.o: core_v5.h

$(OUT)/libandesim_runtime.a: $(LIB_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

$(OUT)/andesim.ld: andesim.ld | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

$(OUT)/andesim.specs: andesim.specs | $(OUT)
	cp $< $@

# gcc adds <-B prefix>/include to the include path, so the two-flag user
# command resolves #include <andesim/ROI.h> with no extra -I.
$(OUT)/include/andesim/ROI.h: ROI.h | $(OUT)
	mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	cp $< $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(OUT)

Verdict: clean on the efficiency axis. No redundant multi-second rebuild, no hot-path waste, no recomputation introduced. Details below, including the specific items you asked about.

## Checked - not issues (with why)

**`driver/cmd_run.cpp:178` - `elf_xlen` in `run_fast` is NOT wasted under an explicit `--engine`.**
The result is still consumed: when `--engine qemu32/qemu64` is given, `xlen` comes from the engine, but `elf_w` then feeds the conflict warning at `cmd_run.cpp:183` (`if (!cli.engine.empty() && elf_w && elf_w != xlen)`). So in every non-empty-positional case the value is both read and used - there is no "computed but unused" path. Deferring it would drop the warning feature. Cost: one `open()` + 16-byte `read()`, once, on a cold path that then execs QEMU (which mmaps the whole ELF anyway). Not worth changing.

**`driver/elf_syms.cpp:124-136` - `elf_xlen` does NOT slurp; it is the efficient outlier.**
It opens an `ifstream` and reads exactly `EI_NIDENT` (16 bytes), then `memcmp`s the magic. Its five sibling readers (`resolve_pc`, `elf_entry`, `elf_load_top`, `symbolize`, `fn_range`) all go through `read_elf64_header` -> `slurp()` (whole file into a vector). The new function is the cheapest ELF reader in the file - exactly right.

**Single ELF read per invocation across modes.** `cmd_run` (`cmd_run.cpp:563-565`) dispatches to exactly one of `run_fast`/`run_accurate`/`run_hybrid`, and each calls `elf_xlen` at most once (`:178`, `:308`, `:410`). No mode reads the ELF twice via the new code, and the modes are mutually exclusive, so there is no cross-mode double-read.
- Note (pre-existing, not this commit): `run_hybrid` already slurps the whole ELF 1-2x - `resolve_pc` (pc-trigger) at `:342` and `elf_load_top` at `:379` - before the new 16-byte `elf_xlen` at `:410`. The added read is 16 bytes on top of two full-file reads that already happen, so it is in the noise. The arch check can't move earlier to fail-fast because it needs `acc->xlen` from the post-discovery engine. Nothing to fix here within this commit's scope.

## Test scripts / Makefiles - no redundant rebuild

**`tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh` - `build_driver.sh` call is the established convention, not new waste.** 17 sibling test scripts call it the same way; it is the standard bootstrap, and `cmake --build` is incremental (no-op when nothing changed). Section C's `make -C tests/fixtures rv32` builds the rv32 runtime + fixtures exactly once.

**`tests/fixtures/Makefile:156-170` - `make rv32` is incremental, does NOT rebuild the runtime each invocation.** The grouped target `$(VPLAT_RT32) &:` has the runtime sources as prerequisites and the five real output files (`build/runtime/rv32/...`) as outputs; make skips the sub-make when those outputs are newer. The `rv32` phony only aggregates two real `.elf` targets, which are mtime-checked. A second `make rv32` with nothing changed is a near-instant no-op. The rv32 target also doesn't touch any rv64 artifact.

**`runtime/Makefile:50` - rv64 path is byte-identical, so no spurious rebuild.** `CFLAGS := $(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall` expands for rv64 to `-march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall` (same as before), and rv64 `OUT` stays `../build/runtime`. The parameterization does not relocate or recompile existing rv64 objects.

**`scripts/build_runtime.sh` / `test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh` - building both arches is the feature/the test, and each `make` is incremental.** Different toolchains, different `OUT` dirs, no double-build. `build_all.sh runtime` now does rv64+rv32 (vs rv64 before), but rv32 is gated on `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` and is incremental; the rv64 lib it produces is reused by `build_all.sh fixtures` (no rebuild).

## One marginal optional (low value)

**`scripts/build_runtime.sh:41,46` - the two arch builds run sequentially and each `make` omits `-j`.** The rv64 and rv32 builds are independent (separate toolchains/output dirs) and each compiles 3 tiny objects. Cheaper: `make -j ... &` both arches concurrently, or at least add `-j` so the 3 objects compile in parallel. Cost saved: ~1s on a cold build only (incremental thereafter), on a build-time script - micro-optimization, not a real redundant rebuild. Mentioning only for completeness; I would not bother.
